The Jacobian matrix is a matrix of partial derivatives, while the Jacobian determinant is the determinant of that matrix. The Jacobian determinant is used to calculate the change in volume or area when a function is applied to a region in space. Another common mistake is forgetting to take the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant when using it to calculate volumes or areas, as the determinant can be negative.
